text:
anna-eng: quick dump — seeing steady VRAM growth on longctx runs with PagedAttention when prefetch_bias=1.0 on H100, but MI250x seems to hold stable. repro steps below.

ben-runtime: can you paste the exact run command and the kernel selection logs?

anna-eng: run: `./run_longctx --model redwood-7b --seq 8192 --prefetch_bias 1.0 --batch 1 --device h100`
logs (snippet):
```
[kvcache] page_alloc: allocating page id=0x7fffc size=2MB
[kvcache] prefetch bias=1.0 window=64 reuse_window=128
[kernelselect] selected=tiling_v2 for seq<=2048
[kv_pager] evict_cand_count=0 reuse_hits=2
```
ben-runtime: that `evict_cand_count=0` is suspicious — means pager didn't consider any pages for eviction even as pagefaults rose?

ciara-ml: mi250 run for comparison? numbers?

anna-eng: MI250x run: `./run_longctx --device mi250`
logs: `prefetch bias=0.25 window=32 reuse_window=96`, and `evict_cand_count` toggles as expected, memory plateau after ~120s.

dave-sre: did you check NVLink/PCIe interconnect behavior? H100 nodes we saw higher dma stalls last week.

anna-eng: yes, traced DMA stalls — small bumps but not enough to explain leak. attaching profiler lines:
```
GPU: H1000
kernel: tiled_attn_v2  dur=1.2ms  memcpy_async wait=0.9ms  dma_stalls=80us
kv_prefetch kernel dur=0.8ms  enqueue_backpressure=10us
```

evans-profile: Looking at perf counters, reuse_window counter increments but the page_table shadow stamp isn't updated when prefetch_bias is aggressive. suspect double-enqueue of prefetches leads to phantom references.

ben-runtime: that matches a race I've seen: prefetch path increments live refcount but the page_table owner tag update gets skipped if kernel_select picks tiling_v2 (fast path) vs fallback. Essentially ownership write gets reordered.

ciara-ml: can we add an assert to the pager that validates owner_tag monotonicity? cheap check: on page fetch completion assert(owner_tag >= last_seen_tag) and log if not.

anna-eng: added quick patch locally:
```
// debug only
if (page->owner_tag < page->last_observed_tag) {
  log("owner_tag rollback", page->id, page->owner_tag, page->last_observed_tag);
}
```
ran with prefetch_bias=1.0 and now we see repeated "owner_tag rollback" entries correlated with VRAM growth.

ben-runtime: nice. Does the rollback only occur when kernel_select chooses tiled_attn_v2?

anna-eng: yes — when forcing kernel_select=fallback_serial the rollbacks disappear and memory stabilizes.

ciara-ml: possible root cause: the tiled kernel uses a different completion callback ordering and doesn't always flush pending KV updates before returning. On H100 that reorder interacts with nvlink transfer coalescing. MI250 kernel path uses explicit barrier.

dave-sre: we should add a short-term mitigation: force prefetch_bias<=0.5 for h100 nodes and add a canary to detect owner_tag regression.

evan-profile: I'll prepare a microbenchmark to reproduce the ordering: run tiled_attn_v2 with synthetic page churn and instrument timestamps on page_table updates vs dma completion. will post results.

ops-bot: deployment note — pinned h100 fleet config: prefetch_bias=0.5 (temp), rollout id=rbw-evict-2026-03-20 :thumbsup:

anna-eng: thanks. Next steps: evan to produce microbenchmark, ben will draft a minimal kernel ordering fix (ensure kv write-back completes before prefetch completion callback), ciara to add owner_tag monotonicity check in debug builds, dave to roll prefetch_bias change to prod h100 fleet.

ben-runtime: one more thought — kernel selection heuristic should consider page_table coherence cost. maybe prefer barriered kernels when prefetch_bias>0.8. I'll prototype a cost model.

ciara-ml: logging note — capture `reuse_window`, `evict_cand_count`, `owner_tag` deltas in the per-request trace so we can build a heatmap.

anna-eng: ok thanks all — will keep thread updated with evan's microbench. current least-priv reproduction attached to bug tracker: https://redwood/issue/INF-1248

evan-profile: microbench attached: confirmed owner_tag write often lags by ~1-3 callbacks on H100 tiled path; MI250 shows 0 lag. will upload traces to the issue.
